title: The Ascension
hook: forty days after Easter; in many places moved to Sunday

segments.voice: Yesterday, Fatima and three children in a world war. Your line was pray for peace. Which place did you name? Day six hundred sixty-nine.

An apprentice's last day goes like this. For years you've worked beside the master, watched his hands, handed him tools. Then one morning he gives you the keys, says the shop is yours, and walks out. You stand there holding the keys, staring at the door. That's roughly where the disciples are at the start of the Acts of the Apostles. Forty days after Easter, on a hill outside Jerusalem, they're staring at the sky. Two strangers in white have a question for them. Today, the Ascension.
screen: `THE KEYS TO THE SHOP.` → `FORTY DAYS AFTER EASTER.` → `STARING AT THE SKY.`

segments.voice: Luke tells it twice, at the end of his Gospel and at the start of Acts. Acts says that for forty days after his passion Jesus showed himself alive and spoke of the kingdom of God. Then, on the Mount of Olives, he tells them they'll be his witnesses to the ends of the earth, and while they watch, he's lifted up and a cloud takes him out of their sight. And then the two men in white, in the Douay-Rheims: "Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven?" It's almost funny. Stop looking up. There's work down here. Mark's Gospel ends the same way, with the apostles going out: "But they going forth preached every where: the Lord working withal." Catholics believe the Ascension is not Jesus leaving the world, but the risen Christ, body and all, entering the glory of the Father, and from there sending the Spirit. The forty days count from Easter Sunday, so the feast falls on a Thursday, Ascension Thursday. But in many places, including much of the United States, the bishops have moved it to the following Sunday so that more people can keep it. Counted from the Thursday, nine days remain before Pentecost. Acts says the disciples went back to the upper room with Mary and the women and kept praying together, and tradition says those days of prayer gave Catholics the novena, nine days of prayer. The master has handed over the keys. The work is theirs now, and he promised not to leave them alone with it.
screen: `FORTY DAYS, THEN A CLOUD.` · `WHY STAND YOU LOOKING UP?` · `THURSDAY, OR MOVED TO SUNDAY.` · `NINE DAYS OF PRAYER TO PENTECOST.` · then, large: `YE MEN OF GALILEE, WHY STAND YOU LOOKING UP TO HEAVEN?`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look up, then look around. If you can, go to a window or step outside. First, look up at the sky for a few breaths. Clouds, blue, gray, a ceiling if that's what you have. Then lower your eyes and look around you, slowly, at what's actually here: the street, the room, the people, the dishes in the sink. Ask one question: what here is mine to do? If you pray, you can ask for help with it. The bell holds the time.
The Ascension. Forty days after Easter, the risen Jesus taken up into heaven before the apostles' eyes. Kept on a Thursday, or in many places the following Sunday. Today's word.
Your line: the work is ours now. Today, do the one thing you noticed was yours to do, before you've finished wishing someone else would. Day six hundred sixty-nine.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Ascension forty days after Easter, on a Thursday, or where bishops have transferred it, on the following Sunday; many then pray a novena to the Holy Spirit in the days before Pentecost.

what a scholar hears: Luke tells it twice, with forty days in Acts; tradition takes the nine days of prayer before Pentecost as the pattern for the novena.

notes: Luke 24:50 places the Ascension near Bethany; Acts 1:12 implies the Mount of Olives. Both on the same ridge; confirm phrasing.
US: most ecclesiastical provinces transfer the Ascension to the Seventh Sunday of Easter; a few keep Thursday. Confirm 'most'.
Novena origin in Acts 1:14 / the nine days between Ascension and Pentecost: traditional explanation; confirm.
Mark 16:20 Douay-Rheims wording; confirm exact text.
